1.

The present claim petition is based on Detailed Accident Report (DAR) filed under section 159/166 clause (4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as Act) by the investigating officer of FIR No.33/2019 Police Station Pandav Nagar, Delhi.
2.
The accident in the present case took place in the intervening night of 17/18.02.2019.
Rahul Jain and Yash Kumar Gupta were going from Vikas Marg towards Mangal Bazar side on their scooter registration No. DL-7SCG-7972.
Rahul Jain was driving this scooter and Yash Kumar Gupta was sitting as pillion.

When they reached near Solitare Hotel, Vikas Marg, a car (Honda City)
registration No. DL 8CAF- 6873 driven by its driver respondent no. 1 Fatehjeet Singh, in a rash and negligent manner, hit their scooter.
Due to this accident, they both fell down on the road.
The car after the accident collided with the divider of the road.
Public persons present nearby apprehended respondent no. 1 and also beaten him.
The injured were taken to the hospital for treatment.
Rahul Jain died on the next day on 19.02.2019.
The petitioners herein are the parents of Rahul Jain and his sister.
It is the case of the petitioners that Rahul Jain was working as Data Entry Operator with Competition Commission of India and was earning around Rs.20,000/- per month.

3. The respondent no. 1 & 2 filed their joint reply alleging that they have been falsely implicated in this case and that that the respondent no. 1 holds a valid driving licence and that the vehicle was duly insured with respondent - SBI General Insurance Co. Ltd.
4.

The respondent no. 3 insurance company - SBI General Insurance Co. Ltd. has taken the general defences and had filed a legal officer initially of Rs.14,29,440/-, which was later on revised to Rs.24,61,232/-.
On 26.02.2020 this amount was released to the petitioners as interim compensation on the ground that it was the admitted amount of the insurance company.
This order of interim compensation was challenged before the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.

On 14.12.2022, the interim award was set aside on the ground that once the legal offer was rejected by the petitioners, they were not entitled for the amount quoted in the legal offer as interim compensation.
5. Because the insurance company has accepted its liability to pay the compensation and because the only dispute remained was regarding the quantum of compensation, regular issues were not framed.

Petitioners were dispensed with the responsibility to prove negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle in the accident and because the revised legal offer was filed taking in view the salary of the deceased in Competition Commission of India, only one issue was framed as the controversy narrowed down only to the fact that whether the deceased was a permanent employee or not.

On 26.02.2020, the following issue was framed :-
(i) Whether petition was a permanent employee.

sentences.text:
On the basis of the evidence led by the petitioners, the quantum of compensation is hereby decided as follows :-
7.
Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

The compensation in the present case is computed as follows : -
ASSESSMENT OF INCOME OF THE DECEASED:
8.
The mother of Rahul Jain has examined herself as PW-1.

According to her evidence, he was a graduate and was working as Data Entry Operator in Competition Commission of India, New Delhi through Orion Security Pvt Ltd, who was the contractor of the deceased.

entities.text: Competition Commission of India, New Delhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Rahul Jain was earning around Rs.20,000/- per month.
9. Petitioner examined Devender Prasad, Deputy Director, Law, from Competition Commission of India.
According to his evidence, the recruitment of data entry operator was outsourceed through Orion Security Pvt Ltd.

He has proved the agreement between them Ex.PW2/A.
10.
Petitioners also examined a witness from Orion Security Bidyadhar Sethi as PW3.
He has proved the register of wages of the deceased from March 2017 till February 2019.
He also proved the salary slips according to which the monthly income of Rahul Jain in January 2019, a month before his death was Rs.19,354/-.

These documents have convincingly proved that Rahul Jain was employed with the Competition Commission of India and through the evidence of PW2, it has been proved that he was in the regular employment.
Therefore, it has been established that the monthly income of the deceased was Rs19,354/-.

APPLICATION OF MULTIPLIER:
11. The date of birth of the deceased as per his aadhar card Ex.PW1/7 is 13.11.1990.
Therefore, the age of deceased was around 29 years at the time of accident on 18.02.2019.
Accordingly, the multiplier of 17 which is applicable to age group of 26-30 years shall be applicable in this case.

FUTURE PROSPECTS:
12. Since the deceased Rahul Jain was in regular employment of the Orion Security Solution Pvt Ltd as per the evidence of PW-2, therefore, he can be considered in permanent job for the purpose of adding future prospects to his salary.

As the deceased came in the age group of 26-30 years, future prospects to the tune of 50% shall be added to his income in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors.

sentences.text: Since the deceased was unmarried at the time of accident and did not have the large family to support, therefore half of the income of deceased has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
CALCULATION OF LOSS OF DEPENDENCY:
14. The monthly income of the deceased has been assessed at Rs.19,354/-.
This means that the annual income of the deceased was Rs.19,354 x12= Rs.2,32,248/-.
After adding future prospects at the rate of 50%, this yearly income will become Rs.3,48,372/- (Rs.2,32,248/-+Rs.1,16,124/-).
After deduction of 1/2 of his personal & living expenses amounting to Rs.174186/-, the yearly income will remain as Rs.1,74,186/- (1/2 of Rs.3,48,372/-).
Applying the multiplier of 17, the loss of dependency is computed as Rs.29,61,162/- (Rs.1,74,186 x17).

NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
15.

In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court, dated 31.10.2017, in case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors. (AIR 2017 SC 5157), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium,
loss of estate and funeral expenses and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors. (AIR 2017 SC 5157)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, a compensation of Rs. 44,000/- each is given to the parents of deceased as filial consortium.
Additionally Rs.16,500/- each on account of loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.
Thus, a sum of Rs.1,21,000/- (44,000x2+16,500+16,500) is granted under this head.

16. In view of above, petitioners shall be entitled for total compensation i.e., Rs.30,82,162/-
(29,61,162+ 1,21,000).

17. The compensation can now be summarised as under :-

 Loss of Dependency after Rs.29,61,162/-
 applying multiplier of 17  Filial consortium Rs.88,000/- (Rs.44,000x2)
 Conventional Heads Rs.33,000/-

 of estate  Award Rs.30,82,162/-
18.
The insurance company has taken much pains to prove that the parents of the deceased had received certain benefits with respect to the death of their son.

Through a witness from EPFO, it has been proved that Rs.2,34,066/- was paid to the mother of deceased Rekha Jain under Employee Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI) and that the father of the deceased is getting a monthly pension of Rs.2901/-.
This is due to the provident found amount deducted from the salary of the deceased.

A witness from ESIC proved that Rs.10,000/- were paid to the father of the deceased as funeral Rekha Jain & Others vs Fatehjeet Singh And Others on 4 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3959310/
4 expenses.

sentences.text:
The law is very clear that the kind of deductions referred above does not come within the provision of pecuniary benefits in view of the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Helen C. Rebello vs. Maharastra SRTC (1999) 1 SCC 90, Vimal Kanwar vs. Kishore Dan (2013) 7 SCC 476,
Reliance General Insurance Co. vs. Shashi Sharma (2016) 9 SCC 627 and Sebastiani Lakra and others vs. National Insurance Company Limited and another (2019) 17 SCC 465.

sentences.text: These judgments have clearly laid down that the amount received by the heirs by way of provident fund, pension and insurance cannot be termed as pecuniary advantage liable for deduction.
Therefore, whatever amount the parents of the deceased got from ESIC or EPFO, is not liable to be deducted from compensation.

LIABILITY:
19.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents are liable to pay the compensation amount.

As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured and, in this case, insurance company has not been able to prove that any term or condition of insurance policy was breached/violated by insured, therefore, respondent no.3/ insurance company becomes liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount.

RELIEF:
20.

In view of the findings on above points, I as presiding officer of this Tribunal award a total compensation of Rs.30,82,162/- (Rs.
Thirty Lakhs, Eighty-Two Thousand One Hundred & Sixty-Two only) along with interest @ 6 % per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realisation except for the period mentioned above, in favour of petitioners and against the respondent no.3 SBI General Insurance Co. Ltd.
This award is required to be deposited with this Tribunal within 30 days.
21. Form IV-A and Form-V in terms of Modified Claim Tribunal Agreed Procedure (MCTAP) are annexed herewith as Annexure A & B respectively.
